newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid makes splash in U.S. corporate bond mart.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid makes splash in U.S. corporate bond mart.

text.p: A offering of $1 billion in new corporate bonds by Rite Aid Corp was the main focus of the U.S. corporate bond market on Tuesday, as secondary market trading continued to be light, traders said.
Frank Bergonzi, chief financial officer at Rite Aid, said the offering was increased to $1 billion from the original amount of $600 million as a result of particulary strong demand from investors.
Rite Aid will use the bulk of proceeds from the offering to refinance approximately $890 million of debt it assumed in connection with its recent acquisition of Thrifty PayLess.
Any remaining proceeds will be used to extend the maturity of existing Rite Aid debt, Bergonzi added.

He said, "We are pleased with the demand and ultimately the rates (of the deal). It lets us funnel our efforts fully into the intergration of Thrifty Payless instead of having to worry about additional financing."
The final offering consisted of $350 million of 6.70 percent five-year debt, $300 million of 7.125 percent 10-year bonds and $300 million in 7.70 percent 30-year bonds.
Goldman Sachs & Co acted as lead underwriter for the deal.
A trader at another frim said investor demand was so strong for the Rite Aid offering becuase few issuers from the retail/industrial sector have tapped the market in recent weeks.
"As opposed to the hundreds of millions of dollars of bank and finance paper we've seen recently, investors were jumping at a chance to get this paper."
Elsewhere, Citicorp issued $300 million in capital securities due 2027 at a spread of 120 basis points over the Treasury curve via a Merrill Lynch & Co Inc led syndicate.
Spreads across the investment grade market closed unchanged to Treasuries amid light trading, traders said.
The closing price on the benchmark 30-year Treasury dropped 15/32 to 97-28/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
Prices of high-yield bonds, which tend to lag Treasuries, were off by 1/8 of a point on average, a trader said. This caused spreads on junk debt to tighten around five to six basis points, he noted.
Junk investors focused on trading of new issues on Tuesday as volume in the broader secondary market remained low.

Heartland Wireless Communications Inc's $125 million 14 percent senior notes due 2004 were bid at 102 near mid-session. The deal by the rural wireless cable company priced at par after the market closed on Monday. BT Securities Corp was the underwriter.

TV Filme's $140 million in 12 7/8 percent senior notes traded up by 1/2 a point on Tuesday, after they were priced at par via Bear Stearns & Co Inc on Monday evening. TV Filme is a Brazilian wireless cable services provider.
